questions.title: Streaming Media Track
questions.prompt:
Create a class `MusicTrack` in `MusicTrack.java`:
* **Private fields:** `String trackTitle`, `String artist`, `int durationSeconds`, `int playCount`.

questions.title: GPS Coordinate Waypoint
questions.prompt:
Create a class `Waypoint` in `Waypoint.java`:
* **Private fields:** `String label`, `double latitude`, `double longitude`.
* **Constructor:** `Waypoint(String label, double latitude, double longitude)`.
* **`toString()`:** Return:
  ```
  Waypoint: <label>
  Lat: <latitude formatted to 4 decimal places>
  Lon: <longitude formatted to 4 decimal places>
  ```
  *(Separated by `\n` with no trailing newline)*
* **`equals(Object o)`:** Two waypoints are equal if their coordinates are approximately equal: `Math.abs(latitude - o.latitude) < 0.0001` AND `Math.abs(longitude - o.longitude) < 0.0001`, regardless of label. Return `false` if `o` is `null` or not a `Waypoint`.

Lat: 40.4275
Lon: -86.9170
Close enough: true

questions.title: Industrial Pressure Relief
questions.prompt:
Create an unchecked exception `OverpressureException` in `OverpressureException.java` extending `RuntimeException` with a constructor taking `String message`.

In `BoilerValve.java`, write:
`public static int adjustPressure(int currentPSI, int deltaPSI, int safeLimitPSI) throws OverpressureException`
* If `deltaPSI == 0`, throw `IllegalArgumentException` with message: `"Pressure change cannot be zero"`.
* If `currentPSI + deltaPSI > safeLimitPSI`, throw `OverpressureException` with message:
  `"Rupture hazard: PSI reached <currentPSI + deltaPSI>, limit is <safeLimitPSI>"`.
* If `currentPSI + deltaPSI < 0`, return `0` (cannot have negative absolute pressure).
* Otherwise, return `currentPSI + deltaPSI`.
questions.expectedOutput:
Pressure: 130 PSI
Rupture hazard: PSI reached 165, limit is 150

tests.name: Test 1 [Visible] (Sample Run)
tests.description: Successful PSI adjustment followed by OverpressureException.

tests.name: Test 2 [Hidden] (Zero Delta PSI)
tests.description: deltaPSI = 0 throws IllegalArgumentException.

tests.name: Test 3 [Hidden] (Negative Delta Below 0 PSI)
tests.description: Adjusting from 20 with delta -50 returns 0.

tests.name: Test 4 [Hidden] (Exact Safe Limit)
tests.description: currentPSI + deltaPSI == safeLimitPSI returns safeLimitPSI.

tests.name: Test 5 [Hidden] (Unchecked Exception Type)
tests.description: Verifies OverpressureException extends RuntimeException.

tests.name: Test 6 [Hidden] (Depressurization to Exactly Zero)
tests.description: Delta reducing PSI exactly to 0 returns 0.

questions.testerExpectedOutput:
Pressure: 130 PSI
Rupture hazard: PSI reached 165, limit is 150

questions.title: Encryptable Communication
questions.prompt:
Create an interface `Encryptable` in `Encryptable.java`:
* Abstract method: `String encrypt(int shift);`
* Abstract method: `String decrypt(int shift);`
* Default method: `default boolean testCipher(int shift)`:
  * Encrypts sample text `"JAVA"`, decrypts the result with the same shift, and returns `true` if the decrypted text equals `"JAVA"`, else `false`.

Create a class `CaesarCipher` in `CaesarCipher.java` implementing `Encryptable`:
* **Private field:** `String message`.
* **Constructor:** `CaesarCipher(String message)`.
* Implement `encrypt(int shift)`: shifts only uppercase alphabetic letters (`'A'` - `'Z'`) forward cyclically by `shift` positions. Non-uppercase letters remain unchanged.
* Implement `decrypt(int shift)`: shifts uppercase letters backward cyclically by `shift` positions (`shift` is positive).
* You may assume `shift` is between 1 and 25.

*(Note: `testCipher` constructs its own `CaesarCipher("JAVA")` internally to validate the round-trip.)*
questions.expectedOutput:
Encrypted: KHOOR
Decrypted: HELLO
Cipher Valid: true

tests.name: Test 1 [Visible] (Sample Run)
tests.description: Caesar shift of 3 forward ("HELLO" -> "KHOOR") and backward, verifying default method.

tests.name: Test 2 [Hidden] (Wrap Around Alphabet)
tests.description: Shifting 'Z' forward by 1 produces 'A'.

tests.name: Test 3 [Hidden] (Wrap Around Decrypt)
tests.description: Shifting 'A' backward by 1 produces 'Z'.

tests.name: Test 4 [Hidden] (Non-Uppercase Characters)
tests.description: Spaces and punctuation like "HI!" keep "!" unchanged ("KL!").

tests.name: Test 5 [Hidden] (Full 25 Shift)
tests.description: Shift by 25 rotates correctly.

tests.name: Test 6 [Hidden] (Polymorphic Reference)
tests.description: Interface reference Encryptable e = new CaesarCipher("TEST"); works seamlessly.

questions.testerExpectedOutput:
Encrypted: KHOOR
Decrypted: HELLO
Cipher Valid: true

questions.title: Blood Donor Eligibility
questions.prompt:
This question gives you a question-specific abstract class **and** a question-specific interface. Your class must extend one and implement the other.

Create an abstract class `Donor` in `Donor.java`:
* **Protected fields:** `String name`, `int age`, `double weightLbs`.
* **Constructor:** `Donor(String name, int age, double weightLbs)`.
* **Getters:** `getName()`, `getAge()`, `getWeightLbs()`.
* **Abstract method:** `public abstract int deferralDays();` (minimum days between donations for this donor type).

Create an interface `Eligible` in `Eligible.java`:
* Abstract methods: `int age();`, `double weightLbs();`
* Default method: `default boolean isEligible(int minAge, double minWeight)`: eligibility requires **both** `age() >= minAge` **and** `weightLbs() >= minWeight` (both inclusive).
* Default method: `default double weightShortfall(double minWeight)`: how many pounds the donor is short of `minWeight`, **never negative** (`0.0` when already met).

Create a class `WholeBloodDonor` in `WholeBloodDonor.java` that **extends `Donor` and implements `Eligible`**:
* **Constructor:** `WholeBloodDonor(String name, int age, double weightLbs)` calling `super`.
* `deferralDays()` returns `56` (eight weeks).
* `age()` returns the donor's age; `weightLbs()` returns the donor's weight.

*Edge cases to think about (not in the sample): the minimum age and weight are inclusive; eligibility is a logical AND — passing one criterion but failing the other must fail; `weightShortfall` must never return a negative number.*
questions.expectedOutput:
Eligible (17/110): true
Deferral days: 56
Shortfall vs 110: 0.0

tests.name: Test 1 [Visible] (Sample Run)
tests.description: An eligible donor, the deferral window, and a zero shortfall.

tests.name: Test 2 [Hidden] (Exact Boundaries Eligible)
tests.description: Age == minAge and weight == minWeight is eligible (inclusive).

tests.name: Test 3 [Hidden] (Fails Age Only)
tests.description: Below minimum age fails even with high weight.

tests.name: Test 4 [Hidden] (Fails Weight Only)
tests.description: Below minimum weight fails even with sufficient age (logical AND).

tests.name: Test 5 [Hidden] (Positive Shortfall)
tests.description: weightShortfall reports the pounds short when under the minimum.

tests.name: Test 6 [Hidden] (Shortfall Non-Negative)
tests.description: weightShortfall is 0.0 (not negative) when the donor exceeds the minimum.

tests.name: Test 7 [Hidden] (Polymorphic Deferral)
tests.description: deferralDays invoked through a Donor reference.

questions.testerExpectedOutput:
Eligible (17/110): true
Deferral days: 56
Shortfall vs 110: 0.0

graderCases.name: Sample run (eligible + types)
Exact age and weight boundaries are eligible
graderCases.body:
WholeBloodDonor d = new WholeBloodDonor("X",17,110.0);
check(d.isEligible(17,110.0), "exact minimums are inclusive");

graderCases.name: Fails age only
graderCases.body:
WholeBloodDonor d = new WholeBloodDonor("X",16,200.0);
check(!d.isEligible(17,110.0), "underage fails despite weight");

graderCases.name: Fails weight only (AND logic)
graderCases.body:

graderCases.name: weightShortfall never negative when over
graderCases.body:

graderCases.name: Polymorphic deferral through Donor reference

questions.title: Parking Garage Structure
questions.prompt:
This question requires a question-specific abstract class **and** a question-specific interface. Every concrete permit must extend the class and implement the interface.

Create an abstract class `ParkingPermit` in `ParkingPermit.java`:
* **Protected fields:** `String permitHolder`, `int semesterWeeks`.
* **Constructor:** `ParkingPermit(String permitHolder, int semesterWeeks)`.
* **Abstract method:** `public abstract double calculatePermitCost();`

Create an interface `Proratable` in `Proratable.java`:
* Abstract methods: `double totalCost();`, `int weeks();`
* Default method: `default double weeklyRate()`: `totalCost() / weeks()`, but **return `0.0` if `weeks() <= 0`** (do not divide by zero).
* Default method: `default double refundFor(int usedWeeks)`: a refund of `weeklyRate()` for each **unused** week (`weeks() - usedWeeks`), **never negative** (`0.0` if `usedWeeks` meets or exceeds the term).

Create `CommuterPermit` in `CommuterPermit.java` **extending `ParkingPermit` and implementing `Proratable`**:
* **Constructor:** `CommuterPermit(String permitHolder, int semesterWeeks)`.
* `calculatePermitCost()`: `$25.00` per week.
* `totalCost()` returns the permit cost; `weeks()` returns `semesterWeeks`.

Create `GaragePermit` in `GaragePermit.java` **extending `ParkingPermit` and implementing `Proratable`**:
* **Private field:** `boolean coveredParking`.
* **Constructor:** `GaragePermit(String permitHolder, int semesterWeeks, boolean coveredParking)` using `super`.
* `calculatePermitCost()`: `$40.00` per week; if `coveredParking` add a `$75.00` surcharge; if `semesterWeeks >= 16` subtract a `$30.00` full-semester rebate.
* `totalCost()` returns the permit cost; `weeks()` returns `semesterWeeks`.

*Edge cases to think about (not in the sample): a 15-week garage gets no rebate but exactly 16 does; `weeklyRate()` for 0 weeks must be `0.0` (never divide by zero); `refundFor` must never go negative when `usedWeeks` exceeds the term.*

tests.name: Test 3 [Hidden] (Exact 16-Week Boundary)
tests.description: Exactly 16 weeks applies rebate.

tests.name: Test 4 [Hidden] (Uncovered Garage)
tests.description: coveredParking = false omits $75 surcharge.

tests.name: Test 5 [Hidden] (Weekly Rate)
tests.description: weeklyRate prorates the total cost over the weeks.

tests.name: Test 6 [Hidden] (Zero Weeks No Divide-By-Zero)
tests.description: weeklyRate(0 weeks) returns 0.0 without dividing by zero.

tests.name: Test 7 [Hidden] (Refund Non-Negative)
tests.description: refundFor returns the prorated unused weeks and never a negative value.

graderCases.name: Sample run (commuter + garage 16wk rebate + types)
15-week garage: no rebate
graderCases.body:

eqD(g.calculatePermitCost(),15*40.0 + 75.0);

eqD(g.calculatePermitCost(),16*40.0 - 30.0);

questions.title: Nuclear Reactor Controller
questions.prompt:
This capstone requires a question-specific abstract class **and** a question-specific interface, extended/implemented together by your concrete class.

Create an abstract class `Reactor` in `Reactor.java`:
* **Protected fields:** `String coreId`, `int temp`, `int coolant`.
* **Constructor:** `Reactor(String coreId, int startTemp, int startCoolant)`.
* **Getters:** `getTemp()`, `getCoolant()`.
* Method `isMeltdown()`: returns `true` when `temp >= 500` **OR** `coolant <= 0`.
* Method `circulate()`: normal circulation raises `temp` by `10` and lowers `coolant` by `5`.
* **Abstract method:** `public abstract boolean injectBoron();`

Create an interface `Coolable` in `Coolable.java`:
* Abstract methods: `int coreTemp();`, `int meltdownTemp();`
* Default method: `default int thermalMargin()`: `meltdownTemp() - coreTemp()`, **never negative** (floored at `0`).
* Default method: `default boolean isCritical()`: returns `true` when `coreTemp() >= meltdownTemp()`.

Create a class `PWRReactor` in `PWRReactor.java` that **extends `Reactor` and implements `Coolable`**:
* **Constructor:** `PWRReactor(String coreId, int startTemp, int startCoolant)` calling `super`.
* `injectBoron()`: if `coolant < 20`, **refuse** — return `false` and change nothing. Otherwise deduct `20` coolant, drop `temp` by `40`, and return `true`.
* `coreTemp()` returns the current temperature; `meltdownTemp()` returns `500`.

*Edge cases to think about (not in the sample): boron injection is refused (no state change) below 20% coolant; injecting with exactly 20% depletes coolant to 0% which is itself a meltdown; `500C` is a meltdown; `thermalMargin` must never go negative when the core is already over the limit.*
questions.expectedOutput:
Temp: 360C | Coolant: 95%
Temp: 320C | Coolant: 75%
Meltdown: false

tests.name: Test 1 [Visible] (Sample Run)
tests.description: Normal circulation heats and consumes coolant; boron injection cools; no meltdown yet.

tests.name: Test 2 [Hidden] (Boron Refused Under 20%)
tests.description: A refused boron injection returns false and leaves temp and coolant unchanged.

tests.name: Test 3 [Hidden] (Boron Exactly 20% to Meltdown)
tests.description: Injecting with exactly 20% coolant depletes to 0% and triggers meltdown.

tests.name: Test 4 [Hidden] (Meltdown at 500C)
tests.description: Temperature at exactly 500C is a meltdown and is critical.

tests.name: Test 5 [Hidden] (Safe Just Below Limit)
tests.description: 499C with coolant remaining is not a meltdown and not critical.

tests.name: Test 6 [Hidden] (Thermal Margin Non-Negative)
tests.description: thermalMargin never returns a negative value, even over the limit.

tests.name: Test 7 [Hidden] (Circulate Effects)
tests.description: Each circulation raises temp by 10 and lowers coolant by 5.

questions.testerExpectedOutput:
Temp: 360C | Coolant: 95%
Temp: 320C | Coolant: 75%
Meltdown: false

graderCases.name: Sample run (circulate, boron, state + types)
Boron refused when coolant < 20 (unchanged)
Boron with exactly 20 coolant depletes to 0 (meltdown)
Meltdown at temp limit 500
Not meltdown just below limit with coolant
thermalMargin never negative
circulate heats and consumes coolant
